title: Mobile-first media queries use min-width
why_it_matters: Phone styles stay simple and desktop adds on top.
explanation: Write your base CSS for small screens, then add min-width media queries to enlarge the layout as space grows. This keeps phone styles simple, and each query only adds the extra rules a bigger screen needs.
try_it: Make a one-column layout that turns into two columns at 768px.

title: Add the viewport meta tag
why_it_matters: Without it phones pretend to be wide desktops.
explanation: Mobile browsers render pages as if the screen were about 980px wide unless you tell them otherwise. This one line in the head makes the page match the device width, so your media queries work.
try_it: Check that every HTML file you made has this tag inside the head.

title: Pick breakpoints from your content
why_it_matters: Layouts break at their own limits, not at phone models.
explanation: Do not choose breakpoints by device names. Widen and narrow the window and add a breakpoint where the design starts to look wrong, such as lines getting too long. Devices change every year, content limits do not.
try_it: Drag your page from 320px to 1200px wide and note where it first looks wrong.

title: Container queries respond to the parent
why_it_matters: A component adapts to its own space, not the screen.
explanation: Media queries look at the viewport, but a card may sit in a narrow sidebar on a wide screen. Mark the parent with container-type, then use @container to style the child by the parent's width.
try_it: Put the same card in a wide and a narrow column and let each choose its layout.

title: Common mistake: no container-type set
why_it_matters: It is the top reason @container does nothing.
explanation: An @container rule only works if an ancestor is declared as a container. Without container-type: inline-size on a parent, the query has nothing to measure and never matches. Also note that the container cannot style itself.
try_it: Add container-type to the parent of a card whose @container rule never applies.

title: Fluid font sizes with clamp()
why_it_matters: Text scales smoothly without breakpoints.
explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) lets a font size grow with the viewport but stay inside limits. Mixing rem and vw in the middle value keeps the text responsive and still respects the user's zoom settings.
try_it: Resize the window and watch the heading grow between 1.75rem and 3rem.

title: transition animates state changes
why_it_matters: Hover effects feel smooth instead of abrupt.
explanation: A transition tells the browser to animate between the old and new value of a property. Set the property, a duration and a timing function on the element itself, then change the value with :hover or a class.
try_it: Add a 200ms transition to a button color change.

title: Avoid transition: all
why_it_matters: It animates things you never meant to.
explanation: transition: all animates every property that changes, including layout ones, which can cause jank and surprise effects. List only the properties you want, such as transform and opacity.
try_it: Replace transition: all in your CSS with the exact properties that change.

title: Quiz: which properties animate cheaply?
why_it_matters: It keeps animations smooth on weak phones.
explanation: Question: which two properties are cheapest to animate? Answer: transform and opacity. The browser can handle them without recalculating layout, so they stay smooth. Animating width, height or margin forces more work.
try_it: Replace a width animation with a transform: scale() animation and compare.

title: @keyframes animate through steps
why_it_matters: You can run animations without any trigger.
explanation: @keyframes defines the steps of an animation and gives it a name. Use the animation property to attach it to an element with a duration. Unlike transitions, keyframes can start on their own and repeat.
try_it: Make a message fade in when the page loads.

title: Debug responsive layouts with device mode
why_it_matters: You test many screen sizes without owning the devices.
explanation: In DevTools, press the device toolbar button to resize the viewport, pick a phone preset or type exact sizes. You can also throttle the network and rotate the screen. Always still test on one real phone.
try_it: Open device mode and test your page at 320px, 768px and 1280px.

title: transform moves and resizes without reflow
why_it_matters: Moving elements this way keeps the layout stable.
explanation: transform moves, scales or rotates an element without changing where its neighbors sit. translate shifts position, scale resizes and rotate turns it. You can chain several functions in one declaration.
try_it: Lift a card by 4px on hover using translateY.

title: transform-origin changes the pivot point
why_it_matters: Rotations and scales grow from the right corner.
explanation: Transforms pivot around the center of the element by default. Set transform-origin to move the pivot, for example top left for a flap that opens like a door, or bottom center for a menu that grows upward.
try_it: Rotate a square around its top left corner instead of its center.

title: scroll-snap makes carousels feel native
why_it_matters: Swipes settle neatly on each slide with no JavaScript.
explanation: Set scroll-snap-type on the scrolling container and scroll-snap-align on the children. With x mandatory, the row always settles on a slide edge, giving a native swipe feel without any JavaScript.
try_it: Build a row of three full-width slides that snap as you swipe.

title: scroll-snap: mandatory vs proximity
why_it_matters: Choose how strongly the scroll is pulled into place.
explanation: mandatory always snaps to a snap point when scrolling stops. proximity snaps only when the scroll ends near one. Use proximity for long content so users are not forced to a position they did not choose.
try_it: Swap mandatory for proximity on a tall page and see how the feel changes.

title: Transparent colors with the slash syntax
why_it_matters: Alpha works in every modern color function.
explanation: Modern color functions put the opacity after a slash, like rgb(0 0 0 / 50%). The same pattern works in hsl, oklch and others, and uses spaces instead of commas. It reads more clearly than the older rgba form.
try_it: Make a 50% black overlay and a 20% blue tint using the slash syntax.

title: oklch makes colors easy to adjust
why_it_matters: Equal lightness steps actually look equal.
explanation: oklch describes a color by lightness, chroma and hue. Changing lightness gives shades that look evenly spaced, which is hard in hsl. It is supported in all current major browsers.
try_it: Make three shades of one color by changing only the lightness number.

title: color-mix() builds shades in CSS
why_it_matters: Hover colors follow your brand automatically.
explanation: color-mix() blends two colors in a chosen color space. Mixing your brand color with black or white creates hover and border shades from one variable, so changing the brand updates every shade.
try_it: Create a darker hover color for a button using color-mix with black.

title: Dark mode with prefers-color-scheme
why_it_matters: Your site follows the visitor's system setting.
explanation: The prefers-color-scheme media query detects whether the system uses a light or dark theme. Put your colors in custom properties, then override them inside the dark query. One change updates the whole site.
try_it: Switch your operating system theme and see your page follow.

title: color-scheme styles built-in controls
why_it_matters: Scrollbars and form fields match your theme.
explanation: color-scheme: light dark on :root tells the browser your page supports both themes. Form controls, scrollbars and default backgrounds then switch automatically. Without it, a dark page can still show bright white inputs.
try_it: Add color-scheme and check how a text input looks in dark mode.

title: light-dark() picks a color per theme
why_it_matters: It replaces a whole media query for simple cases.
explanation: light-dark() takes two colors and returns the first in a light theme and the second in a dark one. It needs color-scheme set on the page. Write both values in the same declaration, no media query.
try_it: Rewrite a small dark mode media query using light-dark().

title: font-display: swap avoids invisible text
why_it_matters: Readers see text while a custom font loads.
explanation: With a custom font, browsers may hide text until the file arrives. font-display: swap shows a fallback font first, then swaps in your font. Pick a fallback with similar proportions to reduce the visible jump.
try_it: Throttle your network in DevTools and see whether your text is visible while the font loads.

title: Outline everything to debug a layout
why_it_matters: You see every box and find the one that overflows.
explanation: When a layout misbehaves, temporarily outline every element. Unlike borders, outlines take no space, so they do not change the layout. You quickly spot which box is wider than its parent.
try_it: Add this rule, find the widest element, then delete the rule.

title: Media queries can test more than width
why_it_matters: You can adapt to touch, contrast and orientation.
explanation: Beyond width, media queries detect orientation, hover support and user preferences like prefers-contrast. (hover: hover) is true for mouse users, so you can keep hover effects for them and avoid sticky hover on touch.
try_it: Wrap your hover effects in (hover: hover) and test on a phone.

title: Project idea: a responsive pricing section
why_it_matters: It exercises queries, grid, color and motion.
explanation: Build a pricing section with three plan cards. Stack them on phones and place them in a row on wide screens. Add a hover lift, a highlighted middle plan and a dark theme using custom properties.
try_it: Sketch the phone and desktop versions on paper before writing any CSS.
